0.tag: Programmes that change how people work
intro: From a single workshop to a national summit, we design the content, run the logistics and report on what changed. Our largest programme to date was convened with federal partners and reached youth leaders across the country.
Training is also built into every other division. When we install a system, your operators learn to run it before we leave site.
steps: Scope and audience
Who is being trained, what they need to be able to do afterwards, and how success will be measured.
Design and content
Curriculum, materials, facilitators and the schedule, built around the audience rather than an off-the-shelf deck.
Delivery and logistics
Venue, equipment, registration, catering and the run of show — on site or at our facilities.
Report and follow-up
Attendance, assessment results and a written report, plus follow-up sessions where the programme calls for it.

1.tag: Systems built, secured and kept running
intro: We cover the full stack: the network and hardware underneath, the software on top, the security around it, and the analytics that make sense of what it produces.
Deployments come with as-built documentation, an asset register and operator training, so your team is not dependent on a vendor for routine work.
steps: Survey and requirements
Site walk, inventory of what exists, and a written statement of what the system has to do.
Design and specification
Architecture, bill of materials and a costed proposal you can take to procurement.
Build and deploy
Installation, configuration, data migration and testing, with progress reporting throughout.
Support and maintain
Defined response times, scheduled maintenance and a named engineer who knows your deployment.

2.tag: Power that does not depend on the grid
intro: Solar and wind systems sized against an actual load profile, plus larger industrial projects including methanol and bio-ethanol plants.
We measure consumption before specifying anything. An undersized system disappoints within a month and an oversized one wastes capital that was hard to raise.
steps: Load assessment
Metering and analysis of what the site actually consumes, by hour and by season.
System design
Array, storage and inverter sizing, structural checks and a projected output figure you can hold us to.
Installation and commissioning
Mounting, wiring, protection, testing and handover with full documentation.
Monitoring and maintenance
Output monitoring, scheduled cleaning and servicing, and battery health reporting.

3.tag: Protection you can audit, not just install
intro: Access control, CCTV, alarms, perimeter and fire systems — specified for the site, installed properly and maintained on a schedule rather than after an incident.
Elevators and escalators sit in the same life-safety regime and need the same inspection discipline, so we handle those too.
steps: Risk and site assessment
Walk the site, identify exposure and agree what the system needs to prevent or record.
System specification
Camera positions, coverage maps, door schedules, detection zones and a costed bill of materials.
Installation and integration
Containment, cabling, devices and head-end, integrated so one operator can see everything.
Testing and scheduled service
Commissioning tests, operator training, and a maintenance schedule with documented inspections.

4.tag: Build the station, then fill the schedule
intro: The technical side — designing, installing and managing terrestrial and online audio and visual broadcast stations — and the editorial side: content development, programme production and digital distribution.
Media consultancy for organisations that need to reach a public audience but have no intention of running a station themselves.
steps: Consultancy and strategy
Audience, platform and format decisions before any equipment is specified.
Studio and station build
Acoustics, equipment, transmission chain and online infrastructure, installed and tested.
Content and production
Programme formats, production schedule and the crew to deliver them.
Distribution and management
Transmission, online distribution, archiving, and ongoing station management if you want it run for you.

5.tag: Groundwork, and the systems that monitor it
intro: Nurseries, orchards and watershed work, plus smart agriculture: sensing, monitoring and data collection on working farms.
Sanitation operations including the establishment and management of toilet facilities for public and commercial sites.
steps: Site and soil assessment
Survey, soil testing and water availability, with a written statement of what the site can support.
Plan and specification
Species selection, layout, irrigation and the monitoring to be installed.
Establishment and build
Planting, infrastructure, fencing and installation of sensing equipment.
Management and monitoring
Ongoing maintenance, yield and condition reporting, and adjustment as the site matures.

6.tag: Estates with the services designed in
intro: Smart residential estates, farm estates and mixed-use developments — designed, built, managed and developed.
Because we also deliver power, security and connectivity, those services are specified at design stage instead of being retrofitted after handover at twice the cost.
steps: Land and feasibility
Title checks, site survey, and a feasibility study covering cost, demand and services.
Masterplan and design
Layout, unit mix, services routing and approvals, with energy and security designed in from the start.
Construction and services
Civil works, buildings, roads, drainage, power, security systems and connectivity.
Handover and management
Allocation, documentation, and ongoing facility and property management services.

All trades coordinated under one contract
